headline: EU Cyber Resilience Act Live, Ransomware Peaks, Critical Flaws Exploited
summary:
This daily cybersecurity digest highlights key developments, including the operationalization of the EU Cyber Resilience Act's 24-hour reporting mandate for digital product manufacturers. The Act's Single Reporting Platform is now live, requiring timely vulnerability and incident reporting.  In parallel, ransomware attacks have reached an all-time high in August 2026, with the utility and healthcare sectors particularly affected.  New threats include a vishing campaign targeting Microsoft 365 users for data theft and a wiper malware deployment by the pro-Ukrainian 'Hacking Cat' group.

Critical vulnerabilities remain a focus, with Microsoft's September Patch Tuesday addressing 974 vulnerabilities, including numerous unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) flaws impacting services like DNS, MSMQ, DHCP, SSTP, and Kerberos. CISA has added five actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, including a JFrog Artifactory vulnerability.  A critical GitLab path traversal vulnerability (CVSS 10.0) is also being widely exploited shortly after its disclosure.  Separately, a breach at Australian education platform Mathspace affected over one million users due to a Metabase vulnerability.

In defensive advancements, Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has developed a behavioral clustering model to map cloud identities, enabling continuous threat detection by analyzing cloud audit logs. This research translates complex behavioral patterns into portable SQL queries for identifying anomalous activities.

articles.headline: EU Cyber Resilience Act's 24-Hour Reporting Mandate Starts Sept 11
articles.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act Reporting Rules Effective Sept 11, 2026
articles.excerpt: Manufacturers of connected products sold in the EU must comply with the Cyber Resilience Act's (CRA) new reporting obligations starting September 11, 2026. The rules mandate reporting actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents affecting their products to ENISA within 24 hours.
articles.updateSummary: ENISA has officially launched the CRA Single Reporting Platform, making mandatory vulnerability and incident reporting effective as of September 11, 2026.
articles.updateContent: The EU Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) has officially launched its Single Reporting Platform, fulfilling the mandate of the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). As of September 11, 2026, manufacturers of products with digital elements must use this portal to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents within 24 hours. This operationalizes the CRA's reporting obligations, providing a centralized system for compliance. Additionally, open-source software stewards will be subject to these rules starting in late 2027.

articles.headline: Vishing Campaign 'PREY-0058' Targets Execs for M365 Data Theft
articles.title: Vishing Campaign Targets M365 Executive Accounts
articles.excerpt: A data theft and extortion campaign, tracked as PREY-0058, is targeting corporate executives using a sophisticated attack chain. Attackers use voice phishing (vishing) to impersonate IT help desks, directing victims to an adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing site to steal Microsoft 365 session tokens. The group then uses residential proxies to access cloud accounts (SharePoint, OneDrive) and exfiltrate data for extortion. The campaign shows overlaps with the threat actor UNC6671.
articles.updateSummary: New phishing lures using 'passkey' themes via calls/SMS to personal phones target M365 users for credential theft.
articles.updateContent: A new variant of social engineering attacks targeting Microsoft cloud users has emerged, leveraging calls and SMS messages to personal phones. Attackers impersonate IT support, urging victims to 'update' their passkey, MFA, or SSO settings on convincing phishing sites. This leads to credential harvesting, account takeover, and data exfiltration, similar to previous campaigns. The campaign, observed since May 2026, broadens the scope beyond executives to general Microsoft cloud service users, highlighting evolving lures and communication channels for credential theft.

articles.headline: Microsoft's Record September Patch Tuesday Fixes 974 Vulnerabilities
articles.title: Microsoft Patches 974 Flaws, Two Exploited Zero-Days in Record Update
articles.excerpt: Microsoft has released its largest-ever Patch Tuesday, addressing 974 CVEs across its product portfolio. The update includes patches for two actively exploited zero-day elevation-of-privilege vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880. Both flaws, which allow attackers to gain SYSTEM privileges, have been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating urgent patching for federal agencies. The release also fixes 113 critical vulnerabilities, including several 'wormable' RCE bugs in core Windows services.
articles.updateSummary: New details emerge on Microsoft's Patch Tuesday, highlighting over 20 unauthenticated RCEs including critical Kerberos flaw, with enhanced hunting hints and workarounds.
articles.updateContent: Further analysis of Microsoft's September Patch Tuesday reveals over 20 unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, expanding beyond the previously noted DNS Server RCE. New critical RCEs include CVE-2026-69579 (MSMQ), CVE-2026-69845 & CVE-2026-72979 (DHCP), CVE-2026-73009 (SSTP), and notably, CVE-2026-69676 (Kerberos), posing a direct threat to Active Directory. The update also provides enhanced hunting hints (e.g., MoUsoCoreWorker.exe monitoring, specific event IDs for DNS/DHCP/MSMQ/Kerberos) and new workarounds like disabling non-essential services or restricting network access.

articles.headline: CISA adds five actively exploited flaws to its KEV catalog
articles.title: CISA KEV Catalog Adds Five Exploited Flaws
articles.excerpt: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added five actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to patch them on a tight deadline. The flaws affect JFrog Artifactory (CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-82329), ConnectWise ScreenConnect (CVE-2026-84869), and MikroTik RouterOS (CVE-2026-67277, CVE-2026-86060). These vulnerabilities pose significant risks, including remote code execution and administrative control, and CISA urges all organizations to prioritize remediation.
articles.updateSummary: CISA KEV update now includes CVE-2026-42018 for JFrog Artifactory, replacing CVE-2026-82329, detailing data leakage impact and new detection guidance.
articles.updateContent: The CISA KEV catalog update for JFrog Artifactory now lists CVE-2026-42018 (CVSS 7.5) as an Improper Authentication vulnerability leading to sensitive data leakage, replacing the previously noted CVE-2026-82329. The update also provides enhanced detection and response guidance, including D3FEND mappings for log analysis and network monitoring, to help organizations identify and mitigate exploitation attempts across all listed vulnerabilities.

articles.headline: GitLab CVSS 10.0 vulnerability exploited one day after disclosure
articles.title: GitLab CVSS 10.0 Flaw Exploited in the Wild
articles.excerpt: GitLab is urging users of self-managed instances to immediately patch a critical path traversal vulnerability, CVE-2026-85706, which holds a maximum CVSS score of 10.0. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files on the server, including credentials and source code. Active scanning and exploitation attempts were detected just one day after GitLab released patches. CISA has added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog, mandating a short patching deadline for federal agencies due to the high risk of widespread, indiscriminate attacks.
articles.updateSummary: New details on active exploitation of GitLab CVE-2026-85706 include HKCERT confirmation, detailed hunting hints, and SIEM detection rules.
articles.updateContent: Further details on the actively exploited GitLab path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) have emerged. The Hong Kong Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre (HKCERT) has also issued an alert confirming widespread exploitation. New cyber observables and hunting hints are provided, including specific log sources like `gitlab-workhorse/current` and `production_json.log`, and target files such as `/etc/gitlab/gitlab.rb`. A detailed SIEM detection rule (YAML) is included to identify exploitation attempts, alongside guidance on EDR monitoring for suspicious process activity. Mitigation strategies are further elaborated with D3FEND mappings, emphasizing immediate patching, network access restriction, and configuration hardening.

articles.headline: Ransomware Attacks Hit All-Time High in August 2026
articles.title: Global Ransomware Attacks Surge to Record High
articles.excerpt: Global ransomware attacks reached a new peak in August 2026, with a record 997 incidents reported, a 23% increase from July. According to data from Comparitech, this averages to 32 attacks per day. The utility sector was hit particularly hard, with attacks doubling, while the healthcare sector saw a 30% rise. The Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware gangs were the most prolific, collectively responsible for over a quarter of all attacks. The Clop group also resurfaced, linking attacks to a vulnerability in PTC Windchill.

articles.headline: Mathspace Breach Affects 1M Users via Metabase Flaw
articles.title: Mathspace Data Breach Hits Over 1 Million Users
articles.excerpt: The Australian education platform Mathspace has disclosed a data breach affecting over one million users. Attackers gained access to an internal reporting database by exploiting CVE-2026-72898, a known SQL injection vulnerability in a self-hosted instance of the open-source business intelligence tool, Metabase. The compromised data includes user names, email addresses, and location information. The company stated that more sensitive data like passwords and academic records were not impacted.

articles.headline: Pro-Ukraine 'Hacking Cat' Group Deploys Wiper Malware
articles.title: Hacking Cat Group Uses Wiper Malware on Russia
articles.excerpt: The pro-Ukrainian hacktivist group 'Hacking Cat' has reportedly escalated its cyber operations against Russian organizations by deploying custom-built malware, including destructive data wipers. The group's stated goal is to disrupt Russian military logistics. This shift from simple disruption or data leaks to the use of destructive malware marks a significant tactical evolution. The incident also highlights the challenge of attribution, as researchers note an overlap in tools used by Hacking Cat and other pro-Ukrainian groups, and the group itself has disputed some public attributions.

articles.headline: Unit 42 Develops Model to Map Cloud Identities via Behavioral Clustering
articles.title: Behavioral Clustering Model Maps Cloud Identity Roles from Audit Logs
articles.excerpt: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has published research on a new behavioral clustering model that uses unsupervised machine learning to analyze cloud audit logs. By examining over 40,000 identities in AWS environments, the model, which leverages UMAP and HDBSCAN algorithms, successfully maps entities to their functional roles, such as administrators or DevOps tools. A key outcome of this research is the ability to translate these complex behavioral patterns into lightweight, portable SQL queries. This allows organizations to implement continuous, scalable threat detection to identify anomalous activities and masquerading threats without the overhead of a persistent machine learning pipeline.
